text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres confident that Portugal will join the Economic and Monetary Union in 1999. Says the escudo will not weaken the Euro.
- Portuguese lorry drivers cut highway near border post of Vilar Formoso to protest against the Spanish truck strike.
- Portugal objects to the final declaration at the European Union ministerial meeting with the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) in Singapore.
- Fernando Pinto dos Santos, Portuguese consul in Hong Kong warns that China will quickly repress liberties in Hong Kong, kicking up polemic with China shortly before President Jorge Sampaio visits.
- Seventy-five percent of Portugual's elite back a referendum on the single European currency says a study by the ISCTE- Instituto Superior de Ciencias do Trabalho & da Empresa.
- Antonio Martins, former chairman of Sines harbour authority, will be new chairman of Lisbon metro company.
- Private mobile phone company Telecel posts 7.3 billion escudo profit in 1996, 204 percent more than 1995.
